requirements.text: The system should be deployed with development and maintenance fully outsourced to an external company, and should support data localization capabilities to comply with jurisdictional data residency requirements.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder indicated the entire development and maintenance should be outsourced and that storage and computing should be handled externally via cloud services.

requirements.text: The system should provide a mobile application for referees and fans, and a web-based application for IFA administrators and team administrators.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder explicitly stated referees and fans should use mobile apps, while IFA and teams use web-based applications.

requirements.text: The system should provide real-time responsiveness with priority for referees during games, while other users experience response times of 1-2 seconds, and should handle up to 50,000 concurrent users.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder specified performance requirements: 50,000 simultaneous users, 1-2 second response for most, real-time priority for referees.

requirements.text: The system should support automatic reminders and alerts based on configurable policies.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder mentioned auto reminders for report submissions and pre-game alerts, implying a requirement for scheduled notification and alerting functionality.

requirements.text: As an unregistered user, I want to view final game data without logging in, so that transparency is increased.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder explicitly stated that even guests should be able to see final game data to promote transparency.

requirements.text: As an IFA administrator, I want to manually override the generated schedule with a documented rationale, so that the change is transparent and requires approval by another IFA representative.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder described the need for manual adjustment of schedule with explanation and second approval to ensure transparency.

requirements.text: As an IFA administrator, I want the system to provide real-time updates from referees during matches, so that I can monitor game events as they happen.
requirements.rationale: Spk 1 explicitly states the main contract is real-time updates from the referee (c81), and Spk 1 confirms a live recording feature is a good idea (c83), indicating a need for real-time data flow.

requirements.text: The system should support data residency to comply with local data regulations.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder mentioned legal restrictions on data storage location (e.g., Germany).

requirements.text: As an IFA administrator, I want to define budget policies and receive alerts when potential violations occur, so that I can monitor financial regulations.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder explicitly mentioned the need to specify budget policy and get alerts for violations.

requirements.text: As a team, I want to insert my own budget transactions and items into the system, so that my team's financial data is recorded.
requirements.rationale: Spk 1 states the insertion of budget transaction and items is done only by the teams.

requirements.text: As an IFA administrator, I want to view all teams' monetary information for monitoring and compliance checking, so that I can ensure adherence to policies.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder specified IFA can view all monetary data for monitoring and auditing.

requirements.text: As a referee, I want to input game events into the system via a mobile application in real time, so that official game data is coherent and reliable.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder explicitly stated referees should insert events in real time via mobile phone, and that this is the only official source of game data.

requirements.text: As a referee, I want to be the only role allowed to insert and update game events, so that the data is coherent and reliable.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder stated only referees can update game events to ensure data reliability.

requirements.text: As a system, I want each game event to have a timestamp, the event type, and optionally any additional required information, so that the game record is complete and auditable.
requirements.rationale: Spk 1 says each event will have its timestamp, the event itself, and maybe additional information required for the specific event.

requirements.text: As a user, I want to export game data, so that the data can be shared externally.
requirements.rationale: Spk 2 asks about exporting data and Spk 1 confirms 'Indeed'.

requirements.text: As a team manager, I want to access my team's own data for viewing and analysis, so that I can manage my team's resources.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder stated teams can view and query their own data for analysis.

requirements.text: As an IFA administrator, I want to define scheduling policies, so that the automatic scheduler respects league rules, with the understanding that the generated schedule can be manually overridden in exceptional circumstances.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder explicitly described the need to define scheduling policies as parameters for the algorithm.

requirements.text: As an IFA administrator, I want to define referee allocation policies, so that the system can automatically assign referees to games.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder explicitly described the need for policy-based referee assignment, including examples of constraints.

requirements.text: As a referee, I want to input my availability preferences into the system, so that the scheduling algorithm can take those constraints into account when assigning me to games.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder stated the system should enable referees to install their preferences, such as planned vacation, to be considered during scheduling.

requirements.text: As an IFA administrator, I want any manual schedule override to require a second IFA representative's confirmation, so that changes are transparent and unbiased.
requirements.rationale: Spk 1 said another IFA representative should confirm the change to ensure transparency.

requirements.text: As a fan, I want to subscribe to notifications about specific games, teams, or players, so that I receive push updates on schedule changes, game events, and player posts without having to pull the information.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder explicitly described the need for fans to register and receive push notifications for games, players, and game events.

requirements.text: As a player, I want to update my social network page within the system, so that I can manage communication with fans.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder stated the player has an option to update their social network page and manage communication with fans.

requirements.text: As a team manager or owner, I want to register my team with the IFA by submitting valid documents through the system, so that the team can be approved and managed in the system.
requirements.rationale: Spk 1 describes the process of a team manager approaching the IFA with documents for approval.

requirements.text: As an IFA administrator, I want to appoint referees into the system, so that referees are officially registered to participate in games.
requirements.rationale: Spk 1 says referees are appointed by the IFA representative.

requirements.text: As an IFA administrator, I want to define leagues and seasons in the system, so that the structure of competitions is established.
requirements.rationale: Spk 1 mentions the IFA should be able to define the league and define the season.

requirements.text: As a system, I want to retain all past archives, so that historical data is available for analysis and reasoning.
requirements.rationale: Spk 1 says all past archives should be kept.

requirements.text: The system should support localization and comply with local data residency regulations.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder raised the need for localization and data residency restrictions, citing Germany as an example.

requirements.text: The system should have a response time within one to two seconds for fans, IFA administrators, and team administrators.
requirements.rationale: Spk 1 says a reasonable response time might be a second or two for those users.

requirements.text: As an IFA administrator, I want the system to support the definition of scheduling policies and to automatically generate a proposed schedule based on those policies, which can then be manually overridden with a documented rationale and approval by a second IFA representative.
requirements.rationale: Spk 1 said the system should execute a scheduling algorithm considering policies.

requirements.text: As a system user, I want to register with a user profile, so that I can be identified and access role-specific features.
requirements.rationale: Spk 1 said users should register to be identified; otherwise they are guests.

requirements.text: The system should prioritize referee requests during active games to ensure real-time responsiveness for event reporting.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder specified that referees need 'very fast' real-time updates and should receive high priority over other activities during a game.

requirements.text: The system should provide push notifications to fans who have subscribed to specific games, teams, or players, with a delivery latency within seconds of event occurrence.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder described push notifications as a key improvement for fan experience, including for in-game events reported by referees, implying near-real-time delivery.

requirements.text: The system should support data localization and comply with local regulations.
requirements.rationale: Spk 1 raises the issue of local regulation and mentions German data cannot leave the country.

requirements.text: As a user, I want to register with identification, so that the system can distinguish registered users from guests.
requirements.rationale: Spk 1 says users should register for identification, otherwise they are just guests.

requirements.text: As an IFA administrator, I want a scheduling override to require an explanation of rationale and approval by another IFA representative, so that transparency and bias are minimized.
requirements.rationale: Spk 1 explicitly states override must include rationale and be confirmed by another representative for transparency and bias issues.

requirements.text: As a fan, I want to receive notifications about live game events as reported by the referee, so that I can follow the match in real time.
requirements.rationale: Stakeholder confirmed fans should get notifications of live events reported by referees.

requirements.text: As an IFA administrator, I want the system to allow manual adjustment of the schedule when a game is canceled due to circumstances such as weather or city events, so that the schedule can be updated as needed.
requirements.rationale: Spk 1 explicitly states the need for manual adjustment of the schedule when games are canceled due to weather or city events.

requirements.text: As an IFA administrator, I want the system to keep all past season scheduling archives, so that historical data is available for analysis.
requirements.rationale: Spk 1 explicitly states that all past archives should be kept for reasoning about future events.

requirements.text: The system should encrypt budget data to protect sensitive financial information from leakage.
requirements.rationale: Spk 1 explicitly states that budget data should be encrypted to avoid leakage.

requirements.text: As a fan, I want to view live game events and overall tournament standings within the system, so that I can follow matches without external news portals.
requirements.rationale: Spk 0 describes a fan portal section for live updates from referees and live scores; Spk 1 confirms fans are exposed to referee data so they don't need external news.

requirements.text: The system should support phased implementation with the first phase covering team, league, season setup, referee registration, and fan registration.
requirements.rationale: Spk 1 explicitly outlines a three-phase priority: basic setup first, then budgeting and scheduling, then real-time referee updates (c100, c101), which is a deployment sequence requirement.
